title: Built-in default of the dnssec-validation option flipped from "no" (9.4.x / 9.5.0) to "yes". "yes" only validates when trusted-keys/managed-keys are configured; no built-in root key existed yet, so most unconfigured servers still did not validate.
after: dnssec-validation yes;

title: dnssec-keygen gained default arguments: without -a it generates a 1024-bit RSASHA1 ZSK, or a 2048-bit RSASHA1 KSK with -f KSK.
after: RSASHA1, 1024-bit ZSK / 2048-bit KSK

title: Default number of additional NSEC3 iterations used by dnssec-signzone (-H) reduced from 100 to 10.
after: nsec3iter = 10U

title: A built-in root-zone trust anchor (bind.keys, managed via RFC 5011) was added; it is used only when "dnssec-validation auto;" is configured.
before: no built-in trust anchor; validation needs trusted-keys/managed-keys
after: built-in root key available via "dnssec-validation auto;"

title: CHANGES 4564: built-in managed keys updated to include the upcoming root KSK-2017 (CHANGES 4564 says only "the upcoming root KSK", RT #44579) ahead of the later rollover. Backported to every maintained branch as separate commits.
before: bind.keys without the upcoming root KSK
after: bind.keys with the upcoming root KSK

title: dnssec-keygen and dnssec-keyfromlabel no longer default to RSASHA1 (NSEC3RSASHA1 with -3); -a is mandatory. Scripts relying on the default fail.
after: error: algorithm must be given with -a

title: Built-in default of dnssec-validation changed from "yes" to "auto": validation is on by default using the built-in IANA root trust anchor, with RFC 5011 managed-keys maintenance.
before: dnssec-validation yes; (validates only with explicitly configured keys)
after: dnssec-validation auto; (built-in root key)

title: RSAMD5 (algorithm 1) support removed entirely (a later commit 9b78f78c69, 2025-10-16, "Restore RSAMD5 tag computation", is not a re-enablement).
before: RSAMD5 supported (explicit -a RSAMD5 to generate; validation accepted it)
after: RSAMD5 unsupported

title: ECC-GOST (algorithm 12, GOST R 34.11-94) support removed.
after: GOST unsupported

title: DSA (algorithm 3) and DSA-NSEC3-SHA1 (algorithm 6) support removed; algorithm numbers kept only as name mapping.
after: DSA algorithms unsupported

title: NSEC aggressive cache (synth-from-dnssec) disabled by default in the 9.14 stable branch after a performance problem.
after: synth-from-dnssec no;

title: synth-from-dnssec restored to yes as the default (9.18 line); 9.16 stayed at no.
after: synth-from-dnssec yes;

title: SHA-1 DS/CDS digests are no longer generated by default: dnssec-dsfromkey emits SHA-256 only (was SHA-1 and SHA-256 both), dnssec-signzone dsset files and named-generated CDS records carry SHA-256 only.
after: DS/CDS: SHA-256 only

title: Default RSA ZSK size in dnssec-keygen raised from 1024 to 2048 bits (KSK was already 2048).
after: RSA 2048-bit for both

title: Built-in dnssec-policy "default": a single CSK (KSK+ZSK roles, unlimited lifetime) with algorithm 13 ECDSAP256SHA256, no explicit key size. The built-in policy "none" is the default for zones (dnssec-policy is opt-in per zone).
after: dnssec-policy "default": csk lifetime unlimited algorithm ECDSAP256SHA256

title: kasp default RSA key size: ZSK 1024 -> 2048 (KSK stayed 2048). Only relevant when a policy names an RSA algorithm without a size; the built-in policy uses ECDSAP256SHA256.
after: RSA 2048-bit for both roles

title: dnssec-policy gained "nsec3param"; when given without parameters it defaulted to 5 iterations and an 8-byte salt.
after: nsec3param iterations 5 salt-length 8

title: Default nsec3param parameters in dnssec-policy changed to zero additional iterations and no salt (RFC 9276 / draft-ietf-dnsop-nsec3-guidance).
after: iterations 0, salt-length 0

title: dnssec-dnskey-kskonly default changed from no to yes: with auto-dnssec the DNSKEY RRset is signed only by KSKs.
after: dnssec-dnskey-kskonly yes;

title: dnssec-cds generates SHA-2 DS records by default, avoids copying deprecated SHA-1 records from the child, and derives SHA-2 DS from CDNSKEY when the child publishes no SHA-2 CDS.
before: copies SHA-1 and SHA-2 CDS digests
after: SHA-2 only

title: Default additional NSEC3 iterations of dnssec-signzone reduced from 10 to 0.
after: nsec3iter = 0U

title: dnssec-policy gained "cds-digest-type" (default 2 = SHA-256) and "cdnskey" (default yes). Defaults equal the prior hard-coded behaviour, so publication defaults are unchanged; only configurability is new.
before: CDS SHA-256 and CDNSKEY published without options (per reference.rst text added by 8be61d1845: default yes)
after: cds-digest-type 2; cdnskey yes; (configurable)

title: Revoked root DNSKEY removed from bind.keys. No behavioural change for validation (key is revoked).
after: revoked key removed

title: New IANA root key (key tag 38696; CHANGES subject: "Update bind.keys with the new 2025 IANA root key") added to bind.keys.
after: bind.keys with key 38696

title: Maximum NSEC3 iterations reduced to a fixed 150 (was key-size dependent: 150 for keys <=1024 bits, 500 for <=2048, 2500 for <=4096). Zone configuration above 150 is rejected and validating resolvers treat NSEC3 answers with more than 150 iterations as insecure (GL #2445).
before: max iterations 150/500/2500 depending on smallest DNSKEY size
after: max iterations 150 fixed

title: Validator and dnssec-signzone limit on NSEC3 iterations lowered from 150 to 50 on the main line only (answers above the limit are treated as insecure); dnssec-policy additionally refuses to load any non-zero iteration count (RFC 9276).
after: DNS_NSEC3_MAXITERATIONS 50

title: CVE-2023-50387 (KeyTrap) mitigation in the maintenance branches: DNS message validation stops at the first validation failure; validation work is moved to a separate slow task queue.
after: fail on first validation failure

title: New options capping DNSSEC validations (default 16) and validation failures (default 1) per resolver fetch; validation made asynchronous.
after: max-validations-per-fetch 16; max-validation-failures-per-fetch 1

title: RRSIG refresh 3 days before expiration
before: signatures regenerated when they expire (1.4.0/1.4.1: zone event scheduled at expires_at)
after: signatures regenerated 3 days before expiration (libknot/dnssec/policy.c; NEWS: "3 days before their expiration with the default signature lifetime")

title: default signing algorithm RSASHA256 (first built-in KASP policy)
before: no built-in policy in 1.x (keys generated externally, e.g. with BIND dnssec-keygen, into dnssec-keydir); the 1.99.1 development preview shipped the first default policy with RSASHA512 (8aaba1c99: policy->algorithm = RSA_SHA512, ksk 2048, zsk 1024)
after: keymgr policy default: algorithm RSASHA256 (8), KSK 2048 bits, ZSK 1024 bits (src/dnssec/lib/kasp/policy.c; doc/configuration.rst@v2.0.0:450-458)

title: default signing algorithm ECDSAP256SHA256; default key size 256
after: ECDSAP256SHA256 (13), KSK and ZSK 256 bits; per-algorithm size table: RSA* zsk 1024 / ksk 2048, ECDSAP384 384 (src/dnssec/lib/kasp/policy.c DEFAULT_KEY_SIZES)

title: default RSA key size 2048 for ZSK as well as KSK
before: RSA policies: ZSK 1024 / KSK 2048 (2.1.x DEFAULT_KEY_SIZES); keymgr required an explicit key size
after: dnssec_algorithm_key_size_default(): RSA* 2048, DSA 1024, ECDSAP256 256, ECDSAP384 384 for both KSK and ZSK; keymgr picks it when no size is given (doc/reference.rst@v2.3.0 ksk-size "1024 (dsa*), 2048 (rsa*), 256 (ecdsap256*), 384 (ecdsap384*)")

title: automatic NSEC3 re-salting every 30 days
before: NSEC3 salt fixed once set (2.2.x keymgr policy)
after: policy.nsec3-salt-lifetime default 30 days, nsec3-salt-length default 8, nsec3-iterations default 10 in the schema (doc/reference.rst@v2.3.0:687 wrongly says 5 until 3.0.6)

title: retired DNSSEC keys deleted automatically
before: retired keys stayed in the KASP database
after: retired keys are removed after their remove timestamp

title: RRSIG inception 90 minutes in the past
after: inception = signing time - 90 min, expiration = signing time + rrsig-lifetime (rrset-sign.c RRSIG_INCEPT_IN_PAST)

title: DSA (algorithms 3 and 6) no longer supported
after: DSA removed from the enum; policies with algorithm 3/6 are rejected ("DSA algorithm no longer supported" in conf checks)

title: minimum RSA key size raised to 1024 bits
after: RSA 1024..4096; default stays 2048

title: keymgr-generated KSK is ready by default
before: manually generated KSK waited in the published state
after: keymgr generate ... ksk=yes creates the key in ready state, so submission proceeds immediately

title: cds-cdnskey-publish default always -> rollover
before: CDS/CDNSKEY for the active KSK published permanently (default always since 2.5.0/2.6.1)
after: CDS/CDNSKEY published only during the KSK submission phase (schema.c C_CDS_CDNSKEY CDS_CDNSKEY_ROLLOVER; doc/reference.rst@v2.8.0 "Default: rollover")

title: keymgr ds no longer prints the SHA-1 digest
before: keymgr ds printed SHA-1, SHA-256 and SHA-384 DS records
after: SHA-1 DS omitted

title: libdnssec honours the local GnuTLS crypto policy
before: algorithm support decided by libdnssec alone
after: dnssec_algorithm_key_support()/digest_support() return false for algorithms the system policy disables (e.g. SHA-1 on RHEL 9); signing/validation with such keys fails

title: NSEC/NSEC3/NSEC3PARAM TTL = min(SOA TTL, SOA minimum)
after: NSEC(3) TTL = min(SOA TTL, SOA minimum); NSEC3PARAM TTL follows NSEC3

title: default policy.nsec3-iterations 10 -> 0
before: schema default 10 (src/knot/conf/scheme.c@v2.3.0:166 .. schema.c@v3.1.9); documented as 5 until 3.0.6
after: schema default 0 (schema.c C_NSEC3_ITER); doc/reference.rst "Default: 0"

title: default policy.rrsig-refresh computed; too-low value is a hard error
before: rrsig-refresh default 7 days; too-low values warned
after: default = propagation-delay + zone-max-ttl; zone signing fails with an error (KNOT_EINVAL in knot_dnssec_zone_sign, d8b1e148f) if rrsig-refresh is too low; NEWS overstates this as a configuration-load failure

title: default policy.rrsig-refresh increased by 0.1 * rrsig-lifetime
after: propagation-delay + zone-max-ttl + 0.1 * rrsig-lifetime

title: validation requires remaining RRSIG validity > rrsig-refresh
before: any unexpired RRSIG accepted by zone.dnssec-validation
after: RRSIGs expiring within rrsig-refresh make validation fail (validation re-run as a scheduled event)

title: default policy.nsec3-salt-length 8 -> 0
after: schema default 0; empty salt (notice added in 3.4.3, 7ed353619)

title: NSEC3 iterations capped at 256
after: policy.nsec3-iterations 0..256 (CONF_NSEC3_MAX_ITERS); NSEC3PARAM with more iterations refused in zone updates; NSEC3PARAM changes via DDNS refused

title: default policy.rrsig-pre-refresh 1 hour -> 0.005 * rrsig-lifetime
after: 0.005 * rrsig-lifetime (100.8 min with the 14-day default lifetime)

title: policy.FORWARD validates (forwarding with validation)
before: policy.FORWARD forwarded without DNSSEC validation (NEWS 1.2.0: "policy.FORWARD() doesn't do DNSSEC validation yet")
after: policy.FORWARD validates answers; the old non-validating mode is policy.STUB

title: ta_signal_query module enabled by default
after: module ta_signal_query loaded by default; resolver sends _ta-<keytag> queries

title: aggressive use of DNSSEC-validated cache (RFC 8198) for NSEC
after: NXDOMAIN/NODATA synthesised from cached validated NSEC; no configuration knob

title: ta_sentinel module enabled by default
after: ta_sentinel (draft-ietf-dnsop-kskroll-sentinel-00, later RFC 8509) enabled by default

title: managed trust-anchor file must be writeable; read-only -K and build-time KEYFILE_DEFAULT added
before: -k <file>: TA file; no read-only mode; no build-time default file
after: -k requires a writeable directory (RFC 5011 managed); -K/--keyfile-ro for unmanaged; KEYFILE_DEFAULT build option (empty by default, config.mk)

title: aggressive caching for NSEC3 zones
after: RFC 8198 synthesis also from NSEC3 (non-opt-out); on by default

title: DNSSEC validation enabled by default
before: KEYFILE_DEFAULT empty by default (v3.2.1 config.mk:26 "KEYFILE_DEFAULT ?="); validation only if built with a keyfile or started with -k/-K
after: meson option keyfile_default=root.keys (v4.0.0 meson_options.txt), always loaded by trust_anchors.lua; -k/-K removed; disable with trust_anchors.remove(".")

title: DO (and CD) bit always sent upstream
before: DO bit sent only when the zone was known secure
after: DO+CD sent on every upstream query, iterating or forwarding, even in insecure zones

title: no aggressive caching on minimal NSEC/NSEC3 ranges
before: RFC 8198 synthesis from any validated NSEC/NSEC3
after: ranges covering only the owner name (black lies) are not used for synthesis

title: NSEC3 iteration cap: zones above 150 iterations treated as insecure
before: no cap; any iteration count validated
after: KR_NSEC3_MAX_ITERATIONS 150 (lib/dnssec/nsec3.h@v5.3.1:19); NSEC3 above the cap not cached, zone downgraded to insecure

title: SHA-1 DS digests ignored when a stronger digest is present
before: every DS digest in the set tried
after: SHA-1 DS skipped if the DS RRset also has a supported non-SHA-1 digest (lib/dnssec/signature.c)

title: policy.STUB: no aggressive denial proofs, no +dnssec copied upstream
before: STUB answers could be synthesised from cached NSEC/NSEC3 and forwarded the client DO flag
after: STUB skips RFC 8198 synthesis and does not copy +dnssec from client

title: NSEC3 limits tightened (CVE-2023-50868): iterations 150 -> 50, salt priced in, >8 NSEC3 RRs refused
before: KR_NSEC3_MAX_ITERATIONS 150; no salt-length limit; unlimited NSEC3 RRs per answer
after: kr_nsec3_limited(): a local MAX_ITERATIONS = 50 compared against kr_nsec3_price(iterations, salt_len), plus a per-query budget of 128 / kr_nsec3_price(...). (v5.7.0 used the macro KR_NSEC3_MAX_ITERATIONS 150; the macro is absent at v5.7.1.)

title: per-request crypto-validation budget (CVE-2023-50387 KeyTrap)
after: vld_limit_crypto_remains budget per request; exceeding it fails validation (E2BIG) without retry

title: built-in root trust anchors gain KSK-2024 (key id 38696)
after: etc/root.keys: KSK-2017 + KSK-2024 (38696)

title: NSEC3 limits tightened (CVE-2023-50868): iterations 150 -> 50, salt priced in, >8 NSEC3 RRs refused
before: KR_NSEC3_MAX_ITERATIONS 150; no salt-length limit; unlimited NSEC3 RRs per answer
after: kr_nsec3_limited(): a local MAX_ITERATIONS = 50 compared against kr_nsec3_price(iterations, salt_len), plus a per-query budget of 128 / kr_nsec3_price(...). (v5.7.0 used the macro KR_NSEC3_MAX_ITERATIONS 150; the macro is absent at v5.7.1.)

title: per-request crypto-validation budget (CVE-2023-50387 KeyTrap)
after: vld_limit_crypto_remains budget per request; exceeding it fails validation (E2BIG) without retry

title: built-in root trust anchors gain KSK-2024 (key id 38696)
after: etc/root.keys: KSK-2017 + KSK-2024 (38696)

after: configure.ac@NSD_2_0_0_REL:333-340 defines DNSSEC unless --disable-dnssec; RRSIG/NSEC added to answers when DO is set

title: DNSSEC compile default flipped to off on trunk
after: configure.ac@NSD_2_2_0_REL:331-338: DNSSEC defined only with --enable-dnssec

title: DNSSEC enabled by default (compile-time)
after: configure.ac@NSD_2_3_1_REL: --disable-dnssec to turn off; DNSSEC (RFC 4033-4035) always compiled in unless disabled
date_note: row released (release commit dc1c5047) used; tag NSD_2_3_0_REL is manufactured on a 2005-01-10 commit

title: dnssec default changed process-no-validate -> process (first release whose default validates on client request)
after: dnssec=process: validate when the client sets AD or DO (dig sets AD); SERVFAIL on bogus; NOT validate for all queries

title: Positive and negative trust anchor management (configured TAs, runtime add-ta/add-nta)
before: only the built-in root DS was usable
after: trust anchors and negative trust anchors configurable via Lua config and rec_control (runtime, volatile); not RFC 5011

title: Ed25519 (algorithm 15) signature validation hooked into the Recursor
after: algorithm 15 validated when built with libsodium (sodiumsigners.cc); algorithm 16 (Ed448) only via optional libdecaf build, not default

title: Built-in root trust anchor gains the 2017 KSK (key tag 20326)
nsec3-max-iterations introduced, default 2500
after: nsec3-max-iterations=2500: NSEC3 records above the cap are treated as Insecure

title: signature-inception-skew setting: 0 in 4.1.5 backport, 60 seconds default in 4.2.0
before: RRSIG inception in the future rejected without tolerance
after: inception tolerated up to 60 s (4.2.0+); 4.1.5+ default 0 s (no tolerance)

title: Built-in root trust anchor drops the 2010 KSK (key tag 19036)
after: rootDSs = {20326}

title: Aggressive use of DNSSEC-validated cache (RFC 8198) on by default: aggressive-nsec-cache-size=100000
after: aggressive-nsec-cache-size=100000 (0 disables); used when dnssec is process/log-fail/validate

title: nsec3-max-iterations default lowered 2500 -> 150
after: nsec3-max-iterations=150

title: Algorithms 5 (RSASHA1) and 7 (RSASHA1-NSEC3-SHA1) switched off automatically when the crypto library refuses SHA-1 signatures; dnssec-disabled-algorithms setting added
before: all implemented algorithms attempted; SHA-1 failures on strict crypto policies (e.g. RHEL9) became Bogus/failed
after: dnssec-disabled-algorithms="" means auto-detect: algorithms 5 and 7 tested with DNSCryptoKeyEngine::verifyOne at startup and switched off when the test fails (treated as unsupported => Insecure); can be set explicitly

title: nsec3-max-iterations default lowered 150 -> 50
after: nsec3-max-iterations=50

title: KeyTrap (CVE-2023-50387/50868) validation limit max-rrsigs-per-record introduced, default 2
after: max-rrsigs-per-record=2

title: KeyTrap (CVE-2023-50387/50868) validation limit max-nsec3s-per-record introduced, default 10
after: max-nsec3s-per-record=10

title: KeyTrap (CVE-2023-50387/50868) validation limit max-signature-validations-per-query introduced, default 30
after: max-signature-validations-per-query=30

title: KeyTrap (CVE-2023-50387/50868) validation limit max-nsec3-hash-computations-per-query introduced, default 600
after: max-nsec3-hash-computations-per-query=600

title: KeyTrap (CVE-2023-50387/50868) validation limit aggressive-cache-max-nsec3-hash-cost introduced, default 150
after: aggressive-cache-max-nsec3-hash-cost=150

title: KeyTrap (CVE-2023-50387/50868) validation limit max-ds-per-zone introduced, default 8
after: max-ds-per-zone=8

title: KeyTrap (CVE-2023-50387/50868) validation limit max-dnskeys introduced, default 2
after: max-dnskeys=2

title: Built-in root trust anchor gains the new KSK (key tag 38696)
DNSKEYs without the Zone flag, and DNSKEYs with the REVOKE bit set, are no longer used to validate
before: any DNSKEY with protocol 3 and matching tag/algorithm was a candidate validation key
after: getByTag() skips keys where (flags & 256)==0 (RFC 4034 s2.1.1) and, in the same commit, keys with the revoked flag (flags & 128, RFC 5011 s3)

title: validation on by default (module-config "validator iterator")
after: module-config default "validator iterator" (util/config_file.c); validation is performed once a trust anchor is configured (none is built in)

title: NSEC3 iteration cap introduced with NSEC3 support
after: val-nsec3-keysize-iterations default "1024 150 2048 500 4096 2500"; higher iteration counts make the zone insecure

title: harden-dnssec-stripped on by default
before: no check that DNSSEC data is present for zones under a trust anchor
after: cfg->harden_dnssec_stripped = 1: answers under a trust anchor that lack DNSSEC data are bogus

title: bogus-ttl default 900 -> 60 seconds
after: bogus results cached 60 s

title: RSASHA256/RSASHA512 disabled by default (--enable-sha2 needed)
after: algorithms 8/10 compiled out unless --enable-sha2 (configure.ac)

title: RSASHA256/RSASHA512 (RFC 5702) enabled by default
after: on by default; --disable-sha2 to turn off

title: DNSKEY RRset must be signed by every algorithm listed in the parent DS set (RFC 4035 2.2)
before: a DNSKEY set validated if any DS algorithm verified it
after: the apex DNSKEY set must be signed with all algorithms present in the DS RRset; otherwise bogus

title: GOST (RFC 5933) enabled by default
after: on by default when OpenSSL provides GOST; --disable-gost to turn off

title: algorithm-downgrade protection from DS-signalled algorithms
before: one verifying algorithm sufficed for a chain of trust step (1.4.7 "if one key matches it's good enough")
after: data must be signed with every algorithm signalled in the DS set (also for trust anchors, DLV and 5011); no knob until harden-algo-downgrade (1.5.4)

title: ECDSA (RFC 6605) enabled by default
before: ECDSA P-256/P-384 (algorithms 13/14) not supported (experimental --enable-ecdsa in the same release cycle)
after: on by default; --disable-ecdsa for older OpenSSL

title: RSAMD5 (algorithm 1) disabled
after: RSAMD5 treated as unsupported (zone insecure); contrib/patch_rsamd5_enable.diff re-enables

title: harden-algo-downgrade default yes -> no
before: cfg->harden_algo_downgrade = 1 (option added 1.5.4 for the behaviour introduced in 1.4.8)
after: cfg->harden_algo_downgrade = 0: one verifying algorithm suffices again

title: unbound-anchor built-in root keys gain KSK-2017 (key id 20326)
after: built-in root anchors: KSK-2010 + KSK-2017 (smallapp/unbound-anchor.c)

title: DS digest algorithm downgrade tolerated when harden-algo-downgrade is no (the default)
before: DS digest-type downgrade always refused (1.1.0: "no longer possible to downgrade to SHA1")
after: with harden-algo-downgrade: no (default since 1.5.5) any supported DS digest suffices

title: trust-anchor-signaling (RFC 8145) on by default
after: cfg->trust_anchor_signaling = 1: _ta-<keytag> queries sent to the root

title: root-key-sentinel on by default
after: cfg->root_key_sentinel = 1 (root-key-sentinel: yes)

title: harden-below-nxdomain on by default
after: cfg->harden_below_nxdomain = 1: names under a DNSSEC-secure cached NXDOMAIN are answered NXDOMAIN

title: DSA (algorithms 3, 6) validation disabled by default
before: DSA validated when the crypto library supports it (--disable-dsa since 1.5.9)
after: configure defaults to DSA off (RFC 8624 section 3.1); DSA-signed zones treated as insecure unless --enable-dsa

title: unbound-anchor built-in root keys drop KSK-2010 (19036)
after: built-in root anchors: KSK-2017 only

title: NSEC3 iteration cap lowered to 150 for all key sizes
after: val-nsec3-keysize-iterations "1024 150 2048 150 4096 150" (util/config_file.c, doc/unbound.conf.5.in)

title: aggressive-nsec (RFC 8198) on by default
after: cfg->aggressive_nsec = 1: NXDOMAIN/NODATA/wildcard answers synthesised from cached NSEC/NSEC3

title: SHA-1 refused by the crypto library at runtime makes RSASHA1 zones insecure, not bogus
before: an RSASHA1/RSASHA1-NSEC3-SHA1 signature the library cannot verify fails validation (bogus)
after: when EVP refuses SHA-1 (FIPS, crypto-policies) the algorithm is treated as unsupported, so such zones validate as insecure (validator/val_secalgo.c)

title: KeyTrap (CVE-2023-50387) validation work limits
before: unbounded RRSIG/DNSKEY combinations tried per RRset
after: MAX_VALIDATE_RRSIGS 8, MAX_DS_MATCH_FAILURES 4, MAX_VALIDATE_AT_ONCE 8, MAX_VALIDATION_SUSPENDS 16 (validator/val_sigcrypt.h, validator/validator.h); exceeding them fails validation

title: NSEC3 hash-calculation cap (CVE-2023-50868)
before: NSEC3 closest-encloser proofs hashed every label without a bound
after: MAX_NSEC3_CALCULATIONS 8 per message, MAX_NSEC3_ERRORS -1 (validator/val_nsec3.h)

title: unbound-anchor built-in root keys gain KSK-2024 (key id 38696)
after: built-in root anchors: KSK-2017 + KSK-2024 (smallapp/unbound-anchor.c)

title: NSEC/NSEC3 TTL capped for aggressive use (RFC 9077)
before: cached NSEC/NSEC3 used for synthesis for their full TTL
after: NSEC/NSEC3 TTL limited to the SOA minimum for aggressive-nsec synthesis

title: module-config default "validator iterator" regardless of build options
before: --enable-subnet (and similar) builds defaulted to a module-config that inserted the extra module
after: default module-config is always "validator iterator"; extra modules must be configured explicitly

title: RRSIG count in the scrubber capped (iter-scrub-rrsig: 8)
before: any number of RRSIGs per RRset accepted from upstream
after: cfg->iter_scrub_rrsig = 8: extra RRSIGs dropped by the scrubber

title: validator caps the number of ANY RRsets it validates
before: every RRset in a qtype ANY answer validated
after: number of validated ANY RRsets capped and the validation wait timer shortened

title: Retrap (CVE-2026-85501): val-clean-additional off by default; validation and hash attempt budgets
before: cfg->val_clean_additional = 1 (since 0.5); no per-query budget of validation attempts
after: cfg->val_clean_additional = 0; cfg->val_validation_attempts = 32; cfg->val_hash_attempts = 32 (util/config_file.c at release-1.26.1)
